samples.summary: Indent/outdent/list-toggle logic is duplicated three times and only one copy got the undo unit, so the same user action now answers differently — and the toolbar copy keeps the #1045 data-loss shape
samples.evidence: `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` in `text-editor.ts:2815,2840` were wrapped in `withUndoUnit`, but the byte-for-byte equivalent logic in `editor.ts:3632 indent()` / `3656 outdent()` / `3612 toggleList()` (same `MAX_LIST_LEVEL = 8`, `INDENT_STEP = 36`, same `forEachBlockInSelection` loop) and the third copy in `text-box-editor.ts:1140,1163` were not. Result: Tab / Cmd+] over a 100-item list is one undo unit, while the *toolbar's* indent / bullet buttons over the same selection still issue one `doc.update()` per block — 100 units against Yorkie's 50-entry cap, i.e. exactly the unrecoverable-tail failure the issue is about, reachable through a different button for the same action. The new docs text (docs-collaboration.md, "Not yet every multi-write action") admits this and defers it to #1048, but the divergence is created by this change: before it, all copies behaved identically. The change also had to fix the inline-style path twice (`editor.ts` `applyStyleImpl` and `text-editor.ts` `applyStyleToSelection`), which is the same duplication showing up as double maintenance.

samples.summary: Unrequested scope: a share-link live-revalidation feature and a whole disposal-revocation mechanism are bundled into an undo-granularity issue
samples.evidence: The issue (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md) is scoped to undo units plus the `YorkieDocStore` undo floor, and its Plan/Non-goals mention neither share links nor editor disposal. This diff additionally introduces: periodic share-link re-resolution (`SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, `useQuery` conversion, `isRevokedShareLinkError`), an editor rebuild on `readOnly` flips in docs/notes/slides mount effects, `revocableDocStore`, `EditorAPI.isDisposed()`, `neuterMutations()` reuse at dispose, `YorkieDocStore.dispose()`, and `isDisposed` gates in `image-insert.ts`. These are a coherent second feature (live share-link authority) with its own user-visible behaviour — a live view can now close itself, and an open editor can be torn down and rebuilt mid-session — and belong in their own change/issue rather than riding along; bundling makes the undo fix hard to review and to revert independently.

samples.summary: The canonical share-link design doc is not updated for the new revalidation contract or the disposal-revocation model
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sharing.md` still describes `/shared/:token` as "Resolves the token" once at mount (line 140-149) and documents the docs read-only model as decided at `initialize()` (lines 163-192). This change makes the resolved role a live value (re-resolved every 60 s and on focus, revocation closes the view, a role downgrade rebuilds the editor) and adds a second revocation axis (`dispose()` turning the handed-out `DocStore`/`Doc` read-only via `revocableDocStore`, `neuterMutations`, `isDisposed()`). Grep across docs/ finds no mention of `revocable`, `isDisposed`, `refetchInterval` or a revalidation interval anywhere, and the project's own lessons file records the sharing.md revalidation contract as deliberately skipped. Per CONTRIBUTING/design-doc discipline this belongs folded into sharing.md (and its Security section, which currently claims revocation "immediately invalidates the token" without describing what a mounted client does about it), not left in code comments.

samples.summary: `readOnly` was added to the notes mount-effect deps without the store `dispose()` the docs path got — `YorkieNoteStore` has no dispose, so each rebuild leaves a `doc.subscribe` attached
samples.evidence: `docs-view.tsx` gained `store.dispose()` in its cleanup precisely because the Yorkie document outlives the effect, and `YorkieDocStore`/`YorkieBoardStore`/`YorkieSlidesStore` all have `dispose()` (slides-view.tsx:1216 calls it). `YorkieNoteStore` subscribes in its constructor (yorkie-note-store.ts:143) and exposes no `dispose()`, and notes-view's cleanup only nulls `storeRef`. Now that `readOnly` is in the deps, a downgrade leaves an orphaned subscription on a discarded store — the same hazard the docs change treats as worth fixing, handled inconsistently across the three views. (The repo's own lessons file acknowledges this as knowingly deferred.)

samples.summary: `replaceAll()` still issues two unbatched writes per match, so the #1045 failure mode survives on the Replace All path
samples.evidence: `replaceAll` snapshots once and then calls `replaceMatch` per match, each doing `doc.deleteText` + `doc.insertText` — two `doc.update()`s per match with no `doc.batch()`. Replace All over ~26 matches therefore exceeds Yorkie's 50-entry cap and loses its oldest writes, the same shape the change fixes elsewhere; the fix is the one-line `doc.batch(...)` the rest of the diff applies. Graded minor because the change documents the gap and tracks it (#1048) rather than silently leaving it, but it is a user-visible data-loss path left open in the very release that establishes the rule.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. text-editor.ts:2815 handleIndent and :2840 handleOutdent are wrapped in this.withUndoUnit (defined at text-editor.ts:3874 as this.doc.batch(fn)), while the byte-for-byte equivalent logic in editor.ts:3612 toggleList / :3632 indent / :3656 outdent (same MAX_LIST_LEVEL=8, INDENT_STEP=36, same docStore.snapshot() + forEachBlockInSelection loop) has no batch — grep for batch( in editor.ts yields only lines 1260/1267/1308, the style and link paths. The third copy in text-box-editor.ts:1121/1139/1162 is likewise unbatched. Reachability is real: docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:941/945/953 invoke editor?.toggleList()/editor?.indent() on the EditorAPI, i.e. the unbatched copies, so Tab (batched, one unit) and the toolbar indent/bullet button (one doc.update per block) now answer differently for the same action against Yorkie's 50-entry cap. The repo's own design doc confirms the divergence rather than contradicting it: docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:313-321 says the EditorAPI toggleList/indent/outdent "still issue an unbatched write per block ... they lose their oldest writes exactly as the keyboard paths did before #1045", deferred to #1048. I considered refuting as out-of-scope, since the originating issue's Goal (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md:22-25) is scoped to "every selection-replacing edit" — which indent/list-toggle are not — and the shortfall is documented and tracked, so the acceptance criteria arguably are met and the toolbar exposure is pre-existing. But the duplication half of the finding is verified and matches this lens's major wording (duplicated logic that now diverges and gives two answers to the same question) with a user-visible consequence, so I cannot concretely refute it and the finding stands.
